reports.title: StoneX Group Inc. Reports Fiscal 2026 Fourth Quarter Financial Results

desk.headline: Net operating revenue up 12% to $655.2m but EPS slipped to $0.66, a miss; record full year, no outlook given
results: Net operating revenues rose 12% to $655.2m, but net income dipped 2% to $84.2m and diluted EPS fell to $0.66 from $0.70 as the tax bill jumped 51% and the share count rose 5%.
Commercial was the bright spot: segment income up 66% to $188.1m, with physical contracts (mainly precious metals) up 89% and OTC derivative volumes nearly doubling.

Institutional segment income fell 25% to $98.9m as securities spreads narrowed and a $17.9m mark-to-market loss on Treasury holdings cut interest income; Self-Directed/Retail income fell 56% to $6.4m on lower FX/CFD volumes. Payments income rose 16% to $35.0m.

Record full year: net operating revenues $2.9bn (+43%), net income $525.4m (+72%), diluted EPS $4.15 vs $2.62 and adjusted EBITDA $971.0m (+62%), helped by a full year of the R.J. O'Brien acquisition.
Book value per share rose to $24.24 from $20.25; per-share figures reflect two 3-for-2 stock splits in March and July 2026.

guidance.summary: StoneX gives no financial guidance. The CEO says the integration of R.J. O'Brien, its largest deal, is complete and met its capital and cost synergy targets.

watch: Whether Institutional earnings recover from narrower securities spreads and lower interest on client balances.
The higher tax rate (about 30% of pre-tax profit this quarter vs about 22% a year ago).
Retail FX/CFD volumes, which fell 17% and pushed that segment to a loss after overhead.
